title: Read-out cases of one app
description: verification/readouts/<app>.json: settings an app is mounted at in jsdom, and for each the numbers and fixed strings it must show, each matched to a source that is not the app's own code. verification/check_readouts.mjs validates every case file against this schema, then checks the rules the schema cannot express (named in the descriptions below). Files whose name starts with _ are not case files. From postrank Explorer v1's schema, without predict: v3 apps have no prediction gate, so a case that scripts a prediction is an error (rule predict).

app.description: The app's v3 name: js/apps/<app>.js, the name of its catalog entry (catalog.json apps[].name). The file name is <app>.json. v1 called this field widget.

catalog.description: The app's v3 catalog id (catalog.json apps[].id, such as "1.3"); its presets are the case presets and its caption is the caption line base.js writes. null only for a test fixture, which then gives its module.

module.description: Project-relative path of the ES module that exports mountWidget. Only fixtures (catalog null) set it; a catalog app is js/apps/<app>.js.

from.description: Where the cases came from, for a port: the v1 case file ("postrank-explorer-v1 verification/readouts/noisy-league.json").

case.description: One mount. Exactly one of preset and query (the check enforces this; the app's defaults are written as query ""). A query that sets predict is an error (rule predict), and so is a raw query that sets preset. Every key the query, the preset, the spec or the updates name must be a key of the app, and every query value one the app takes (rule query), so a key renamed in the port or a value it cannot read is reported, not silently ignored.

id.description: Unique within the file; a port may keep v1's case ids.

preset.description: A preset of the app's catalog entry, by its v3 id (catalog.json apps[].presets[].id). The app is mounted at ?preset=<id>, as a reader's link reaches it, and base.js applies the preset; the preset row must then show it pressed (rule preset).

query.description: A raw query such as "?tau=.30&cap=3" (or "" for the defaults), given to the app as window.__PRX_QUERY. It may set theme; not predict and not preset.

spec.description: Optional spec object passed to mountWidget(el, spec). As on a page, base.js applies a preset first, then the spec, then the query's keys.

update.description: Partial specs passed to handle.update() in order after the first render, each one settled (aria-busy included); the expectations read the final state. An update may name a preset by its v3 id ({ "preset": "tau40" }).

expectation.description: One element and where its value comes from. kind number (default unless source is literal): the element itself carries data-num; its raw value must equal the source value within tol, and its text must equal format(raw). kind text: the element text (or the attribute named by attr) must equal value exactly.

select.description: A CSS selector inside the app's mount element. Without index it must match exactly one element. Hooks: [data-prx-readout="<name>"] on a read-out number (keep v1's hook names when porting), [data-prx-label], [data-prx-caption="<id>"], [data-prx-family-size], [data-prx-part~="caption"] for the caption line.

index.description: Pick the n-th match (document order, from 0) when the selector matches several elements.

attr.description: kind text only: compare this attribute (aria-label, title) instead of the text.

slots.description: A literal text of an element only (not an attribute): compare the text with each outermost data-num element written as a slot, as in "Monte Carlo, ⟨S⟩ draws, seed ⟨seed⟩". Any ⟨name⟩ is one slot; the value writes no digit outside its slots. The numbers in the slots are checked by their own expectations (and all of them by the general rules), so a sentence is checked word for word without writing a number into a literal.

format.description: The engine formatter of the element's kind (fn, options, item, spread), as in v1's numbers/spec. Default for registry: the key's own format (verification/v1-registry/spec; settings use formatSetting; case keys their display_format), and then the text must also equal the registry's display string. Required for golden and oracle numbers.

source.description: golden: a postrank 1.1.0 golden row (verification/golden, uses_postrank true); oracle: an independent base-R oracle row (uses_postrank false); registry: a key of v1's frozen numbers registry (verification/v1-registry/numbers.json or numbers-cases.json; the registry is a source of expected values only, never of shown numbers); literal: a fixed string (a label, caption, legend, heading or table caption) only, never a number, whose ref is the row label of the v1 contract rule that fixes it.

ref.description: registry: the v1 key ("six.A.cap3.tau20.risk"); golden and oracle: { group, row, field }; literal: a row id of verification/v1-registry/contract-rows.json such as "6.2" or "11.4" (a 6.2 literal must be a result label and a 6.5 literal a caption of js/shared/labels.js, in their v3 wording).

value.description: The expected value written out (a number, an array, null for NA, a decimal string for a count above 2^53, or the exact string for text). It must agree with the source within tol, so a stale case file fails.

tol.description: Default: the registry entry's tolerance; for golden and oracle the parity tolerance of the group and field (verification/parity.d); 0 otherwise.

field.description: A dot path inside the row's expect object ("pi", "E.0", "krwCard.risk").

fn.description: An engine formatter (js/pr-core.js) or a named format of js/shared/format.js (formatShare, formatExpectedCount; no options).
